source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's CIN2 campus in Cincinnati publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, one of only nine Ohio facilities that disclose a megawatt figure at all.

The pattern here is disclosure, not scale. Ohio has 79 mapped facilities and only 9 publish a megawatt number, so any state total built from those 9, which comes to 118.4 MW, describes the small subset of operators willing to state a figure rather than the state's actual data center load. CIN2's 11 MW ranks fourth within that disclosed set, which makes it mid-sized among the few sites we can measure and unranked among the many we cannot.

For AI specifically, the useful number is the 11 MW of IT load, because that is the input to any rack or accelerator estimate. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density, so the conversion is an outside assumption. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 11 MW is roughly 275 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 1,100. The same electrical capacity supports very different amounts of compute depending on a figure CyrusOne does not provide.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, show the campus is qualified for regulated workloads, but they say nothing about which tenants occupy it, and no tenant names are published. The data also does not cover expansion plans, cooling design, or the generation and transmission capacity behind the 11 MW. It establishes one disclosed input at one campus, and the rest of the picture, including how much of that power actually runs AI hardware, remains unpublished.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
